text:
sam: Quick spike: Go SDK generator doesn't reliably cancel when creds block during token refresh. Repro below (super small).

sam: ```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
creds := &blockingCreds{delay: 3*time.Second}
client := NewClient(WithCreds(creds))
g, _ := client.Generator(ctx, "mini")
go func() { time.Sleep(100*time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
if _, err := g.Stream(ctx); err != nil { log.Printf("stream err: %v", err) }
// observed: handshake goroutine stuck in creds.Fetch; ctx cancel isn't seen promptly
```

rita: Oof. Two UX-safe fixes: (A) require GetToken(ctx) on creds so refresh is cancellable; (B) add a generator.StreamWithContext(handshakeCtx) or generator.Abort() to force teardown.

corey: Idea: add StreamWithContext(ctx) that uses a per-handshake ctx independent from user ctx, so sample apps can do `ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(parent, 5*time.Second)` and pass that in. Also add Abort() as an escape hatch for legacy creds.

sam: I like StreamWithContext for explicitness in sample apps. But for parity we should still change creds API to accept ctx and provide a small shim for old creds to avoid breaking users.

rita: Action items: 1) short-term: add ClientOption HandshakeTimeout default=5s + onboarding README snippet showing StreamWithContext pattern; 2) add generator.Abort() that is safe/idempotent; 3) long-term: RFC to require GetToken(ctx) and publish migration shim with example; 4) add unit test that simulates blocking creds + cancel and asserts no goroutine leak.

ci-bot: [ci] Canary: generator e2e goroutine regression detected; opened INF-6001.

doc-bot: Added a docs TODO: update Go SDK "Cancellation & Streaming" page with StreamWithContext example and migration note.

sam: I'll draft the README snippet and the small sample-app change. Corey, can you prototype Abort() and the handshake-timeout option? Rita will draft the shim and the RFC.

corey: Yep. I'll include a tiny leak-detection test.

sam: Cool, tagging SDK parity board.
